ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, ABCD is a square with a side length of 4. Point H is on the extension of CD, and CEFH is also a square. What is the area of $\triangle DBF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the side length of the square $CEFH$ be $a$,

according to the problem, we have: $S_{\triangle BDF}=S_{\text{square }ABCD}+S_{\text{square }CEFH}-S_{\triangle ABD}-S_{\triangle DHF}-S_{\triangle BEF}$,

$=4^2+a^2 -\frac{1}{2}\times4\times4-\frac{1}{2}a(a-4)-\frac{1}{2}a(a+4) =\boxed{8}$.

method.method_draft: Synthetic same-base/same-height route. First read the diagram: ABCD is the left square with B bottom-left, C bottom-right, D top-right, and CEFH is the right square with C bottom-left and F top-right; triangle DBF is formed by diagonal DB of the left square, point F of the right square, and segment DF. method.method_draft: Area-complement route. Read from the diagram that triangle DBF sits inside the union of the two adjacent squares ABCD and CEFH, and that the remaining parts of this union are triangles ABD, DHF, and BEF. From the text, ABCD has side length 4; let the side length of square CEFH be a, so CH=CE=EF=FH=a. ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, ABCD is a square with a side length of 4. Point H is on the extension of CD, and CEFH is also a square. What is the area of $\triangle DBF$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Let the side length of the square $CEFH$ be $a$. According to the problem, we have: $S_{\triangle BDF}=S_{\text{square }ABCD}+S_{\text{square }CEFH}-S_{\triangle ABD}-S_{\triangle DHF}-S_{\triangle BEF}$, $=4^2+a^2-\frac{1}{2}\times4\times4-\frac{1}{2}a(a-4)-\frac{1}{2}a(a+4)=\boxed{8}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: On the left side of the figure is square ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right; on the right side is square CEFH, with C at the lower left, E at the lower right, F at the upper right, and H at the upper left, and H is on the upward extension of CD. The figure also draws line segments such as DB, BF, DF, and what is required is the area of triangle DBF.

Reasoning: It is known that the side length of square ABCD is 4, so its area is 4×4=16. Segment BD is the diagonal of square ABCD, and segment CF is the diagonal of square CEFH. Since the sides of the two squares are both in the horizontal and vertical directions, diagonals BD and CF have the same direction, therefore BD ∥ CF. Points C and F are both on line CF, so the distances from C and F to line DB are equal. Thus triangles DBC and DBF use the same DB as the base, and their heights are equal, so their areas are equal. Triangle DBC is half of square ABCD, so its area is 16÷2=8. Therefore the area of triangle DBF is 8.
